solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ask again about city devastated by war

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to repeat a question about a war-torn city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals rearranging the letters of ASK AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese port was destroyed by an atomic bomb in August 1945.

clue.text: A dry fish served up for ex-PM

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking alcohol

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the fish word is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A dried fish is put on the table for a former prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: Assessment of King Charles I, quite awful

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher of a King Charles

indicators.note: awful suggests the word quite has been badly mangled, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A historian's damning verdict on the reign of Charles I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charles I' reads as one monarch, but splits into CR (Carolus Rex) and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A critique is a detailed evaluation or review, so it is a synonym for an assessment.

clue.text: Card that is carried by player at St Andrews

definitions.meaning: a playing card of the suit marked with black trefoils

definitions.text: that is carried by player at St Andrews
definitions.meaning: St Andrews is the Scottish home of golf, and a golfer carries sticks to hit the ball

explanation.surface: A golfer at St Andrews has a playing card in their bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a card suit and a golfer's stick for striking the ball.

clue.text: Old coin, say? Right

parts.note: to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an object is an old coin and is told they are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: It's almost twelve — have a sleep

indicators.note: almost means the word for twelve is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: It is nearly midnight, so time for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to nap lightly, so it means to have a short sleep.

clue.text: First sign of weariness shown by worker in need

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer begins to look tired and in need.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and need are synonyms, as in living in want.

clue.text: One of the family, what completes our happiness

indicators.note: what completes a word is its final letter

parts.note: elation is great happiness

explanation.surface: A family member is the final ingredient of a household's joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a relative, a member of one's family.

clue.text: Thelma playing Shakespearean role

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress called Thelma takes a part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is the title character of one of Shakespeare's tragedies.

clue.text: Bishop facing additional worry

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
other can mean additional, as in other examples

explanation.surface: A bishop faces yet another concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother as a noun is trouble or fuss, a synonym of worry.

clue.text: In Paris I must hug a new girl

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap around, so the French pronoun goes around the other letters

parts.note: je is the French word for I

explanation.surface: A Frenchman insists on embracing a girl he has just met.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane is a common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Queen needs a form of transport, something poetic

parts.note: a train is a form of rail transport

explanation.surface: The monarch requires a vehicle, which has a lyrical quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatrain is a four-line stanza of verse, so a poetic thing.

clue.text: Arty type eats with thee in strange fashion

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange fashion, so eats and thee are mixed together

explanation.surface: A pretentious artistic person dines oddly, using old-fashioned speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a refined appreciation of art and beauty.

clue.text: One bringing goods in from exotic trip — Rome?

indicators.note: exotic suggests something unusual or altered, so trip and Rome are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader returns with goods from an exotic holiday in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a person or firm that buys goods from abroad into the country.

clue.text: Type met by head gets consideration

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A sort who meets the boss gets thought given to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness is thoughtful regard for others, a synonym of consideration.

clue.text: Excursions made by rich man around Russia's capital

indicators.note: around means the rich man's name is placed round the letter

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the Bible parable of Lazarus

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, as in a capital letter

explanation.surface: A wealthy man takes outings around Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia's capital' tempts towards MOSCOW but gives only its first letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drives are trips or outings by car, so they are excursions.

clue.text: Look gloomy, as Maureen before gym

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: Maureen looks miserable before her gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to sulk or be listless and dejected.

clue.text: Mucky stuff fellow found on northern river

parts.note: a fellow is a man
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, in northern England

explanation.surface: A man is discovered sitting dirty on the bank of a northern river.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure is animal dung used as fertiliser, so literally mucky material.

clue.text: Volunteers repeated musical phrase as a duty

parts.note: the TA, or Territorial Army, is the British volunteer reserve force
a riff is a short repeated phrase in popular music

explanation.surface: Reservists play the same tune over and over out of obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax or charge on imports, which is a customs duty.

clue.text: A maiden sitting on usually large book

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for an extra-large size

explanation.surface: A girl perches on a big volume.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue A and M sit on top of OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Fine, loose plant

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: A fine plant grows freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the blue-flowered plant grown for linen fibre and linseed.

clue.text: Eager African's first to escape from country

indicators.note: to escape from means the letter gets out of the country's name, leaving it

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An African is keen to be the first to flee a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry can mean keen or avid, as in hungry for success.

clue.text: Agreement in a set of books written by witches

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pact recorded in volumes penned by a coven of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding pact or contract.

clue.text: Bank offers relief — pounds I lost

indicators.note: lost means these letters are taken away from the word relief

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bank offers help after a customer loses money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial but is the definition in its sense of a ridge under water.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the water's surface, a kind of sandbank.
